scope: All existing 50 chapters and 423 sections, plus 12 explicitly assigned repairs; editorial self-review only.

findings.finding: Definitions arrived after their first operational use: single-qubit probabilities, Pauli matrices and Pauli-specific matrix functions.
findings.disposition: State the computational-basis probability postulate in 3.1, define Pauli matrices in 3.3, and keep 2.6 a generic Hermitian-function bridge.

findings.finding: No-cloning required a two-system tensor-product argument before tensor products were introduced.
findings.disposition: Move the existing stable section from 3 to 4, after tensor-product structure; preserve old public anchors.

findings.finding: Selective measurement and ignored records risked an unintroduced or invalid statevector average.
findings.disposition: Limit 6.2 to selective pure-state updates and marginal probabilities; own density mixtures in 8 and mixed-state instruments in 9.

findings.finding: Phase-based amplitude estimation required jumping from 16 to 17 and back.
findings.disposition: Put a phase-free inference example in 16 and move the phase-estimation-based derivation to 17 after QPE; no Chapter 17 prerequisite remains in 16.

findings.finding: The algorithm route lacked Simon’s canonical hidden-structure example and a clear Abelian/discrete-log bridge.
findings.disposition: Add explicit optional/core-scoped sections in 15 and 18 with local binary/group/arithmetic bridges.

findings.finding: Qubitization was named but not assigned its own invariant-subspace derivation.
findings.disposition: Add a selected Hermitian block-encoding walk construction in 20 before spectral transformation applications.

findings.finding: Quantum information comparison did not clearly cover channel error contracts, mixed entanglement or cryptographic no-go boundaries.
findings.disposition: Assign channel metrics/process tomography to 10, mixed-state LOCC/witness/distillation to 12, and a scoped no-go argument to 13.

findings.finding: Calibration and runtime performance risked being confused with experimental device characterization.
findings.disposition: Add SPAM/RB in 28 under explicit model assumptions; keep state/process inversion in 10 and runtime timing in 44.

findings.finding: Modern QEC coverage lacked named quantum-LDPC and bosonic-code homes.
findings.disposition: Add an architecture-aware LDPC section in 30 and an optional oscillator-correction bridge in 34; both require explicit model/error assumptions.

findings.finding: Optical links and modular hardware were named without a shared networking primitive.
findings.disposition: Own pure-state entanglement swapping and classical-message/quantum-link distinctions in 7; mixed-state distillation belongs to 12.

findings.finding: Several whole-chapter prerequisite lists forced unrelated advanced topics before simple entry tasks.
findings.disposition: Replace them with entry guidance and a curated direct-prerequisite graph for every section. Validate compiler, kernel, tensor and memory paths against unnecessary-topic regressions.

findings.finding: Compilers and basic physical models inherited QFT, full hardware surveys or broad fault-tolerance routes.
findings.disposition: Let 41 enter from circuit semantics and 42 from an explicit target contract; physical branches use selected common bridges and advanced controller/logical tracks have separate requirements.

findings.finding: Fixed kernels inherited trainable-layer prerequisites; MPS became an unnecessary gatekeeper for general contractions.
findings.disposition: Create independently checked fixed-kernel and trainable-layer routes; permit general contractions from tensor/circuit tools without 46.

findings.finding: Repeated concepts risked being fully re-taught across foundations, algorithms, hardware, compilation and simulation.
findings.disposition: Record a unique explanatory owner for each recurring concept and mark later uses as applications/reminders, with an explicit duplication matrix.

findings.finding: The full plan’s workload had no quantitative planning bound.
findings.disposition: Assign provisional section page ranges and compute chapter/route totals. Recommend modular/volume packaging review rather than advertising 50 chapters as a single introductory course.

findings.finding: Basic mathematical/physical tools were sometimes assumed under a broad audience promise.
findings.disposition: Assign local probability, calculus, binary algebra, arithmetic/group, oscillator and rotating-frame bridges before use, with exact section dependencies.

findings.finding: Small algorithm demonstrations could imply stronger preparation, verification or complexity claims.
findings.disposition: State eigenstate-overlap cost in QPE, scoped promise/QMA limits in 22 and the expensive tiny-reference boundary in linear-system examples.

findings.finding: Chapter titles had been treated as sufficient evidence of coverage and learning continuity.
findings.disposition: Publish the all-section ledger, chapter-specific decisions and prerequisite-closed routes; require independent specialist/source and reader validation before freeze.

findings.finding: H2 and logical-memory reproduction claims require explicitly bounded scholarly provenance.
findings.disposition: H2-01–09 now traces STO-6G integrals, BK projection, electron sector and 324 coefficients at printed precision; original author integral files were not recovered. Select Fowler et al. v2, Section VII A/Fig. 5 for memory ambiguity; the finite memory benchmark is an extension, not threshold reproduction.

findings.finding: The roadmap still allowed new depth/body pilots before the user’s architecture-first requirement was met.
findings.disposition: Pause new body drafting. Continue architecture, source mapping and validation design only until the baseline gate is satisfied.

chapters.decision: Retain an informal preview with supplied rules; do not pretend formal measurement/evolution has already been established. Revisit the calculation after 3–6.
Remove the premature Pauli specialization from matrix-function introduction. Own linear algebra/norm/tolerance foundations; statistical and physical bridges have named later homes.
State the single-qubit probability postulate before interference/Bloch use. Introduce Pauli matrices before their algebra; move no-cloning to the tensor-product chapter.
Own subsystem/index conventions and now the no-cloning proof after tensor products. Runtime gate kernels are developed in 44 rather than re-derived here.
Retain introductory reversible logic, universality and small identities. Advanced synthesis algorithms and pass correctness are owned by 41–42.
Repair selective versus ignored-outcome language: no averaging statevectors. Introduce probability/independence before estimator claims; full mixed-state instruments belong to 8–9.
Add entanglement swapping/network-resource primitives. Derive no-signalling from marginal probabilities first; mixed-state entanglement is deferred to 12.
Own ensembles, reduced states, purification and unconditioned density updates. Entry does not require completing every protocol or Bell-test topic in 7.
Retain representation equivalence and complete-positivity arguments. This is the channel/instrument owner, not a duplicate physical-noise catalogue.
Add channel/gate comparison contracts and process tomography. Treat shadows and advanced channel norms as optional inference branches; device characterization protocols are owned by 28.
Retain entropy/relative entropy/data processing with explicit support and proof scope. Do not require tomography/shadows before basic entropy.
Add mixed-state entanglement/LOCC/witness/distillation reasoning and distinguish finite experiments from capacity theorems. Keep specialized full capacity proofs as scoped advanced readings.
Scope a complete QKD path and add an explicit cryptographic no-go boundary. Remove the requirement to complete all channel-capacity theory before the protocol entry.
Retain input/output, access, complexity and complete costs plus the hybrid map. Separate comparison assumptions from empirical advantage claims.
Restore Simon’s problem and a local binary-equation bridge. Oracle construction remains explicit; general hidden-subgroup structure is owned by 18.
Replace the forward phase-estimation dependency with a locally introduced phase-free inference method. Move the phase-estimation-based derivation to 17 and preserve its stable ID.
Own QFT/QPE and the phase-based amplitude-estimation extension in sequence. Make eigenstate-overlap/preparation cost explicit; no ground-state-preparation claim follows from QPE alone.
Add an advanced Abelian hidden-subgroup/discrete-log example with a local group/arithmetic bridge. Keep non-Abelian representation theory outside the core route.
Remove the unnecessary QFT/QPE entry requirement for time evolution/product formulas. Retain adiabatic assumptions and operator/state/observable error distinctions.
Add the missing qubitization invariant-subspace derivation between block encodings and QSP/QSVT. Keep access, normalization, conditioning and postselection costs visible.
Retain a complete scalar-to-matrix signal-processing path; one proved application plus explicit advanced theorem scope. Do not duplicate polynomial derivations in the walk chapter.
Separate algorithm design, query lower bounds and Hamiltonian-complexity limits. Add a scoped promise/QMA boundary without turning small optimizer experiments into complexity evidence.
Retain spectral/shared-parameter differentiation with a local calculus bridge. Parameterized tensor contracts are owned here; learning/encoding claims belong to 27.
Remove full state-inference prerequisites from optimizer entry. Geometry, trainability theorems and noisy-gradient arguments are branches with exact section requirements.
Mark the long chemistry/embedding chapter as a core energy/model path plus independent advanced modules. Do not force embedding, dynamics or sampled-subspace methods before the H2 capstone.
Retain objective mapping, alternating circuits and honest solution metrics. Reuse optimization tools from 24 rather than re-teach optimizers.
Make fixed-kernel/feature and trainable-layer paths independent. Fixed kernels must not inherit quantum backpropagation prerequisites; include data-access and evaluation bridges.
Own physical-noise assumptions, calibration and device characterization. Add SPAM/RB with its own local ensemble/model assumptions; runtime timing benchmarks are owned by 44.
Retain the full correction-condition/recovery argument and coherent error-span logic. Teach the first bit-and-phase construction without requiring undeveloped CSS terminology.
Add quantum-LDPC/check/connectivity tradeoffs. Keep three separable branches: stabilizer codes, measurement-based graph states and decoder interfaces; introduce binary/group tools locally.
Retain repeated syndrome circuits, boundaries, decoder and logical failure definitions. Threshold/scaling evidence remains model-specific; shared syndrome algebra is referenced from 30.
Remove factoring and full surface-code prerequisites from the generic logical-gate route. Require surface-code material only for surgery, and retain explicit threshold/magic-state assumptions.
Remove all-algorithm prerequisites. A named logical workload and logical-operation/error models suffice; actual decomposition algorithms remain in 42.
Retain a common physical bridge, now with an optional bosonic-correction module. Do not require QFT, every noise topic or every code family before basic hardware models.
Keep a self-contained effective circuit/transmon branch using selected common physics. Detailed BCS/device fabrication remains out of scope; compiler algorithms are referenced rather than repeated.
Keep the local oscillator/sideband/drive bridge and explicit motion-return/transport costs. Avoid cost-free connectivity assumptions and unrelated algorithm prerequisites.
Retain distinct digital, analog and motion contracts. The adiabatic theorem is developed in 19; a Rydberg device model does not imply arbitrary graph programmability.
Separate optical modes, encoded qubits, conditional gates, graph-state computation and optional CV material. Require only the relevant graph-state/oscillator sections for each branch.
Retain a local effective spin/exchange/readout model with explicit omitted levels. No whole chemistry, Fourier or fault-tolerance route is needed for entry.

Retain a theory-first, evidence-qualified advanced branch. Majorana/fermionic and protection/logical supplements have separate prerequisites; full tensor-category theory is an explicit exclusion. TOPO-01–09 now pins claim-level experimental and source-status cases; subscription comment/reply full-text and independent interpretation review remain open.
Remove microscopic hardware from program/IR entry. Own program semantics, dynamic maps, rewrites and interchange boundaries; optional derivative checks use the differentiation bridge.
Remove whole-platform prerequisites from mapping/scheduling entry: an explicit target contract suffices. Own synthesis/mapping algorithms; logical-set approximation is an optional prepared branch.

Separate control, local dynamic feedback, logical lowering and host workflow tracks. Runtime orchestration must not require pulse optimization, and decoder feedback need not traverse every logical-gate chapter.
Make the minimal exact-state executor accessible before AD and density evolution. Own execution/parallel-runtime benchmarks, not experimental RB error characterization.
Make tableau entry depend on Pauli/stabilizer sections, not all error-correction or numerical-executor topics. Defer magic-resource extensions explicitly.
Retain the SVD/Schmidt-to-MPS argument. Pure-state construction needs neither tomography nor all density/gradient execution; compare truncation with declared metrics.
Remove MPS as a prerequisite for general circuit contraction. Keep contraction and cutting/reconstruction as distinct branches, with all signed-weight/statistical overhead explicit.
Allow scientific specification and paper-reading habits early. Statistical/resource and application tools are selected for a claim rather than requiring whole advanced courses.

Require only the energy/mapping/gradient and research sections needed by the H2 calculation. Source chain and independent reconstruction are checked at printed precision; original author files are unavailable and mathematical/reader review remains open. Embedding/learning are not prerequisites.

Use Fowler et al. v2, Section VII A/Fig. 5 as a precise syndrome-ambiguity source. The finite memory benchmark is a labeled extension, not a threshold reproduction. Dense/enumerated reference avoids a later-tableau prerequisite; resource extrapolation stays optional.
